steps: Plan the design option

Choose standard, vented cavity or Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-052 / KZK-1510), plus up to (2) HTK-EXT / HTK-INT heat transfer kits and, if used, the Kozy Power Vent #KPV. Converting to propane or for the KPV is easier before framing in; after installation the control board has to come out.

• Standard: follow the sections marked 'standard installation'. Standard framing still applies with heat transfer kits; remove (1) square side cover plate per kit (section 3.8, p. 20).
  • Vented cavity: a minimum opening in the fireplace cavity reduces heat above the fireplace, allowing combustible facing above, heat reduction for a TV and lower mantel clearances. Remove the convection baffle and cover plates (p. 21). Front option: a single 3" (76mm) x 52" (1321mm) minimum discharge opening; top option: at least 1-1/2" (38mm) from the enclosure top to the ceiling on all three sides. No grilles or louvers, and at least 60" (1524mm) from the discharge opening to any sprinkler head.
  • Komfort Zone Kit: redistributes radiant heat through plenum(s); framing may differ, so follow the kit manual.
  • Kozy Power Vent #KPV: fan-powered mechanical draft, horizontal terminations only; follow its manual.
  • Chamber and ceiling at least 88" (2235mm) for every option.
  • Out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies, on a level surface that supports the fireplace and venting. It may go in a bedroom, and in an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home where local codes allow.
  • It's heavy: team-lift with the side lift handles (a 2" x 4" fits through them).
  • Outdoor covered installs: operation is approved from 40°F to 110°F; the roof overhang in front and to each side must be at least 1/2 of the roofline height above the fireplace base, and black painted safety barriers are recommended (p. 18).
Nailing flanges & stand-offs

Fit both nailing flanges (they set the 3½" clearance from the fireplace sides to framing), the top stand-off assembly with its header heat shield, and the formed back stand-off heat shields. They stay on whatever the finish material.

• Nailing flanges (all applications): move the (2) flanges from the sides to the holes on the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace, and screw through the slots. Bend the perforation until parallel with the fireplace face, never toward it. Framing studs sit against the small stand-off on the back of each flange.
  • Stand-off assembly (standard and vented cavity): form the header heat shield and attach it with (4) screws, then secure the assembly to the top of the fireplace with (4) screws. Form the back stand-off heat shields and resecure them with the screws you removed.
  • KZK installs: the header heat shield may be removed and discarded, but the top stand-off assembly and the back stand-offs must still be installed (p. 22).

The stand-off assembly sets the minimum distance to the header and is the contact point for non-combustible material above the fireplace.
Frame the enclosure

Minimum rough opening 50-1/2" H x 65-5/8" W x 28-3/4" D, with at least 88" for the enclosure and to the ceiling. Set the unit level on wood or a non-combustible surface, or on a full-size metal or wood panel over carpet, tile or other combustibles.

• Rough framing is the same for every design option (Komfort Zone Kit framing may differ; see the kit manual).
  • Leave room in front for barrier removal, component access, the gas line and service.
  • Insulate outside walls: the enclosure is a cold air transfer area.
  • Floor protection in front isn't required. A combustible hearth extension may be used, flush with the bottom finishing edge.
  • Raised installs need a solid, continuous platform; prepare a foundation for the full load of any masonry.
  • TV above: tests found TV surface temperatures did not exceed 150°F (66°C) with a 4¼" (108mm) deep recess above the fireplace. TV location rests with the homeowner.
The manual also prints the rough opening width as 66 5/8" (1667mm), in Figure 3.4 (p. 14); Table 3.1 (p. 14) and Figures 3.5 (p. 15) and 4.4 (p. 33) give 65-5/8" (1667mm).
Vent pass-through framing

Keep 1" clearance around the vent pipe and 11" between any venting and the enclosure top on horizontal terminations; horizontal sections rise ¼" per 12". A Metal Fab vent needs adapter 5DDA, which raises the minimum pipe centerline 3-1/4".

• 1" (25mm) on all sides of vertical pipe and on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe; 11" (279mm) from any venting to the enclosure top on every horizontal termination.
  • Horizontal sections need ¼" (6mm) rise for every 12" (305mm) of travel.
  • Wall thimbles meeting the 1" (25mm) top clearance are required wherever horizontal pipe passes through a wall. Thimbles and attic insulation shields may be insulated using unfaced insulation listed as non-combustible per ASTM E 136.
  • Elbow heights vary by vent maker; adjust the pass-through opening to keep clearances. Figure 3.7 (p. 17) shows the minimum pass-through framing as a drawing, dimensioned for a Simpson DuraVent elbow.
  • Metal Fab: adapter 5DDA adds 3-1/4" (83mm) to the minimum centerline height. Don't recess the vent cap into the wall or siding.
Facing & finishing

Non-combustible facing up to 1/2" thick at the top and sides, stopping at the finishing edge so the glass frame stays removable; screws may enter the outer shell only 1/2". Combustible mantel trim from 8" and a 6" mantel from 11-1/2" above the top finishing edge.

• Combustible mantels grow 1" (25mm) deeper for every 1" (25mm) higher from the 6" (152mm) mantel. The bottom finishing edge may be flush with a combustible hearth.
  • Non-combustible mantel: at least 6" (152mm) above the top finishing edge for up to 6" (152mm) of depth, then 1" (25mm) up for every 1" (25mm) deeper. 6" (152mm) to any mantel leg and to an adjacent sidewall.
  • Minimum non-combustible finishing areas are shown as a drawing (Figure 4.5, p. 34).
  • Against drywall cracking: dry, dust-free materials; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound such as Durabond, cured to the maker's instructions; a high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish coat. Avoid flat or light-colored paints.
  • Vented cavity and KZK only: a combustible wall finish up to 1" (25mm) thick may go over the required non-combustible material, but must not block the discharge opening (Figures 4.7 and 4.8, pp. 37–38).
Gas line connection

Connect a listed 1/2" tee-handle shut-off valve and flexible connector (3/8" x 24" supplied) to the 1/2" control valve inlet, run through the gas access hole without obstructing the fan. Check all connections for leaks with soapy water.

• A qualified person to local codes, or ANSI Z223.1 where there are none. Massachusetts: a licensed plumber or gas fitter, with a Commonwealth-approved valve.
  • System pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi (3.5 kPa) or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Built for natural gas. The propane conversion kit (LCK-BH52-SPB) is sold separately; follow its instructions, the authority having jurisdiction and ANSI Z223.1.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
Venting & restrictor plate

Run an approved 5" x 8" system (or a 4" x 6-5/8" reducer) within the vertical and combination limits. The included restrictor plate goes into the exhaust pipe before venting, or later through the baffle, when the flame needs vent restriction.

• Approved systems, run limits, elbows and cap clearances: see the Venting and Termination clearances cards.
  • The restrictor plate (components packet) ships with all inner rings intact, giving the most restriction. Knock out the innermost ring for less restriction, or all inner rings for the least.
  • Bend its tabs to about 80° so it holds itself in place. Before venting, slide it into the exhaust pipe on top of the fireplace, tabs facing you; after venting, insert it into the 5" (127mm) exhaust pipe in the firebox ceiling through the baffle (section 11.2.2, p. 67).
  • Vertical terminations may show an active, compact flame; if that look is not wanted, the restrictor plate may need to be installed or modified.
  • Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
Panels & log set

Install the refractory or black glass panels (required to operate) with the (6) clips bent to 90°, then the 17-piece BH52-500 or BH52-B501 log set by the number under each log, never over the burner ports. Convert to propane first.

• Remove the safety screen and glass frame first (never while hot): release the (4) spring-loaded latches with the provided tool, tilt the top of the frame forward and lift it off the bottom rail.
  • Refractory: back panel first, then the sides (tilt the back of the panel in, then pivot up), each with (2) clips.
  • Black glass: smooth side forward, textured side against the firebox; clean gloves and both hands; check each panel lies flat.
  • Logs: log 1 at the rear against the log stop brackets; a thick layer of rock wool embers over the whole burner and ports (steel or stiff nylon brush); logs 2 to 7 on the burner studs; ember panels either side of log 5; logs 8 to 13 on their studs and notches; crushed glass in the ember-bed media tray; logs 14 and 15 on the ember bed; the (6) charred pieces; lava rock at the sides; rock wool on logs and burners.
  • Poor log placement affects the flame and can cause excessive soot on the logs and glass.
Wire & initialize the control

Plug into a grounded 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amp supply that's always hot. With the ON/OFF switch OFF, load (4) AA backup and (3) AAA remote batteries, power the module, sync the remote, then set the switch to ON.

• No switch in the AC supply; shut the breaker off before working on electrical lines. Three-prong plug straight into a properly grounded receptacle.
  • Light kits (power disconnected): with the media tray out, (4) halogen bulbs into the ember-bed lamp bases; (2) into the top light kit #600-TLK. Never touch the bulbs with bare hands.
  1. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox.
  2. Main ON/OFF rocker switch OFF; (4) AA batteries in the backup holder on the control module; (3) AAA in the remote; connect the IFC module to AC power.
  3. Press the remote sync button on the left side: 3 beeps and an amber LED. Within 5 seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: 4 beeps, and the pilot lights.
  4. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out and the system is initialized.
  5. Set the ON/OFF switch to ON for remote operation, and reinstall everything you removed.
Note: 10.2 (p. 59) removes the safety screen, glass frame and gas valve access cover to reach the switch and sync button; 10.3 on the same page removes only the safety screen.
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet pressure at the IN tap (other gas appliances on) and manifold pressure at the OUT tap, then reseal and re-check both taps. Burn at least 15 minutes and compare the flame with the venturi and restrictor guides; venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician.

Factory venturi openings

Natural gasCenter 1/4" (6.35mm) · sides 1/8" (3.175mm)
PropaneCenter 1/2" (12.7mm) · sides 1/4" (6.35mm)

Flames start blue and turn yellow over the first 15 minutes; lazy, yellow flames need no adjustment. Closing the air shutter gives a yellow flame but may soot the glass. Slight venturi changes give dramatic results: adjust in small steps, burn at least 15 minutes and let it cool between adjustments. Soot on the logs? Check log placement first.

Venturi guide (Table 11.4)

  • Dark, orange flame with black tips: venturi closed too far, open it slightly.
  • Short, blue flames: venturi open too far, close it slightly.
  • Lifting (ghosting) flames: gas pressure too high, or venturi closed too far. Check manometer settings; open the venturi slightly.

Restrictor guide (Table 11.5)

  • Short, flickering flame: excessive draft, add the restrictor plate.
  • Lifting or ghosting: insufficient draft, remove inner ring(s) or the plate. Still lifting after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent? Shut off the gas and call a qualified service technician.
Note: p. 66 says opening the venturi air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner (and Table 11.4 says to close the venturi for short, blue flames), but the troubleshooting chart on p. 69 says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or run on the battery backup
Wiring disconnected → check each connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check the shut-off valves; there may be more than one before the main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not enveloping the flame sensor → pilot screw on the valve: clockwise smaller, counterclockwise larger
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten
Pilot always on or won't go out → control set to CPI; set it to IPI

panels.title: Main burner won't light
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch it ON
Gas supply off or low → check for multiple shut-offs; check the propane tank
Faulty or incorrect wiring → see section 9.0
Plugged main burner orifice → remove the blockage
Pilot flame not directed to ignite the burner → see the pilot checks
Remote not working, or no call for heat → replace batteries; remote ON, thermostat operation OFF
No reaction to commands → low batteries, lost remote link (re-initialize, 10.2) or too many failed ignitions (reset, 10.7)

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: No propane in tank → refill
Glass assembly installed incorrectly → section 8.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Wrong pitch on horizontal venting → ¼" (6mm) rise per foot (30cm) required
Exhaust leaking back into the firebox → find and repair vent leaks
Excessive draft → install or modify the restrictor plate (section 11.2.2)

panels.title: Soot on glass · blue, lifting flame
items: Soot from log placement → re-set the logs per section 8.4
Soot from the venturi setting → open the air shutter slightly (section 11.2.1)
Soot from vent cap installation or blockage → adjust; remove debris
Blue flame lifting off the burner → the chart says open the air shutter slightly; p. 66 says opening it causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner (see the flame check step)
Blue, lifting flame from the cap installation, or a blocked or leaking vent → check the pipes for leaks and the cap for debris

codes: Backup pack under 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF commands. Replace the batteries.
No flame after 2 ignition tries. Verify the gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset (10.7.1) or re-initialize (10.2).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an igniter lights the pilot automatically, and the pilot lights the burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Turn it on and off

Press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace beeps once, and about 4 seconds later the igniter starts sparking at the pilot. Press ON/OFF again to turn the fire off.

The manual's full operating instructions

They have you shut off and check the gas first:

  1. Read the safety information first, including what to do if you smell gas.
  2. Press ON/OFF on the remote to turn the fireplace off. Then turn off all electric power to it.
  3. Find the manual gas valve your service technician installed. Turn it clockwise to OFF.
  4. Wait 5 minutes for any gas to clear. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  5. Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON.
  6. Turn the electric power back on and press ON/OFF on the remote.
Won't operate? Turn off the gas to the fireplace: press ON/OFF to turn it off, turn off the electric power if it will be serviced, and turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF. Then call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs on (3) AAA batteries in the bay at its base. A single beep from the fireplace confirms on, off and flame-height commands.

On and off

  • With the fireplace off, press ON/OFF. The screen shows all active icons and the fireplace starts lighting.
  • Press ON/OFF again to turn it off. The screen then shows only the room temperature.

Flame height

There are 6 flame levels. Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one level, all the way to off. The up arrow raises it one step. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow relights it on HI.

Thermostat

  • Press the thermostat key. The screen shows a temperature bulb, the room temperature and the set temperature. Change the set temperature with the arrows.
  • Keep pressing until SMART appears. The flame now turns itself down as the room reaches the set temperature, and you can't change the flame height by hand.

Key lock and °F / °C

Press mode and the up arrow together to lock or unlock the keys; a lock icon shows while they're locked. With the fireplace off, press thermostat and mode together to switch between °F and °C.

sounds.title: That sound, smell or fog is probably normal
sounds.html:
A new gas fireplace has a few habits that are completely normal.

Foggy glass

When you first light it, condensation forms on the glass. This happens with all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell for the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during that time; it helps the paint cure faster.

Ticks and creaks

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, so you'll hear noises of varying degree. That's normal and doesn't affect how well or how long the fireplace works.

Blue flames at first

The flames look blue when the burner first lights and slowly turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. Lazy, yellow flames are what you want. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips (soot), have a qualified service technician check the burner's air setting.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electric switches or use a phone in the building, and leave right away. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass & yearly service
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is the maintenance job the manual gives you. Do it once a year, with the fireplace off and fully cooled.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Release the 4 spring-loaded latches with the tool provided. Tilt the top of the glass frame forward and lift it off the bottom rail.
  4. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Put the glass and the safety screen back before you use the fireplace.
Never clean or remove the glass while it's hot, and don't strike or slam it. Don't run the fireplace if the glass is cracked or broken.

Yearly service

Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year, including the firebox, vent, burner, pilot and glass. A qualified service person should vacuum the fan every 6 months. Lint from carpet or bedding can mean cleaning more often.

Note: the glass removal steps on p. 47 put the 4 spring-loaded glass latches at the top of the firebox; the yearly firebox maintenance on p. 70 says to inspect and operate the bottom latch assembly.

reset.title: Won't light? Reset it
reset.html:
When you press ON/OFF, the fireplace makes up to two tries to light. It sparks at the pilot for about 60 seconds, pauses about 35 seconds, then sparks for another 60 seconds. If no flame is sensed, it locks out and a red light on the control module blinks 3 times, again and again, until it's reset.

Reset a lockout

Press ON/OFF to turn the system off. Wait about 2 seconds, then press it again. The lighting sequence starts over.

What the red light means

1 blinkBackup batteries low. Replace them.
2 blinksPilot flame error. Contact your dealer.
3 blinksLockout. Check the gas is on, then reset.

Quick checks

  • Is the house power on? Are the remote and backup batteries fresh and in the right way round?
  • Is the manual gas valve ON? There may be more than one shut-off between the fireplace and the main gas line. On propane, check the tank.
  • Is the main ON/OFF switch on the left side of the unit set to ON?
  • No call for heat? Make sure the remote is on and thermostat operation is off.
Still won't light? Turn off the gas to the fireplace and call your service technician or gas supplier. The manual's troubleshooting chart is for a qualified technician.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
An igniter always lights the pilot for you, and the pilot lights the burner. You choose what the pilot does between fires.

IPISpark-to-pilot: the pilot lights each time you turn the fire on
CPIContinuous (standing) pilot: stays lit even when the burner is off

A standing pilot keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

Switch modes

  1. With the fireplace off, press mode on the remote until the CPI icon is selected.
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the screen means CPI. No snowflake means IPI.

Good to know

  • Pilot won't go out? It's set to CPI. Switch to IPI.
  • 7-day timeout: in CPI, if the burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off as a safety feature. Lighting the burner starts the 7 days over.
  • A short pause: within 24 hours of continuous pilot flame, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds to check its safety functions, then repeats your last command.

fan.title: Fan, lights & split flow
fan.html:
Press mode on the remote to step to each feature, then use the arrows.

Fan

There are 6 speeds. At the fan icon, the arrows turn the fan on, off, or change its speed.

  • Thermostat mode: the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights, so heat can build first. It keeps running about 12 minutes after the fire turns off.
  • Manual mode: the fan runs at its last setting, with no delay at start or stop.

Split flow

The split-flow icon controls the secondary burner: up arrow on, down arrow off.

Lights

  • Top accent light (light icon): 6 brightness levels with the arrows.
  • Ember-bed light (AUX icon): up arrow on, down arrow off. Its brightness is set with a knob on the left side of the firebox, behind the safety screen and the gas valve access cover. Turn it counterclockwise to dim, clockwise to brighten.
The fan and both lights don't run on the backup batteries in a power outage. Leave the fan off for the first few hours of use while the paint cures.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power. A backup battery pack keeps the burner working in a power outage.

Backup pack (control module)(4) AA, not included
Remote(3) AAA, included

In an outage

Only the burner runs on the backup batteries. The fan, top light and ember-bed light don't. Battery life depends on battery quality, how often it lights, and other factors.

Low batteries

  • Backup pack: the fireplace double-beeps when you press ON/OFF, and the red light blinks once. After that it ignores commands until you replace the batteries. It beeps once when the new ones are in.
  • Remote: a battery icon shows on the screen before the power runs out. It goes away once you replace the batteries.

Manual operation

The manual's section 10.3 sets the system up for manual operation. The ON/OFF switch on the left side of the unit then turns the burner on and off, on HI only.

Note: 10.3 (p. 59) says to remove the safety screen to reach that switch; 10.2 on the same page also removes the glass frame and gas valve access cover, and p. 47 takes off the glass frame before that cover. Never remove the glass while it's hot.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electric switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace and next to the floor; some gas is heavier than air. Use only your hand to turn the gas valve, and never use tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it: call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

Hot glass and children

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety screen on. If it's damaged, replace it with the Hussong barrier made for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely. A safety gate can keep at-risk people out of the room and away from hot surfaces.

Never

  • Burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it, or keep clothing, gasoline or other flammables near it.
  • Run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • Use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s limited lifetime warranty covers the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship. You don't need to send in any paperwork; keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model.

30 days · parts & laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborAll other parts and material
Year 2 to lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is paid to an authorized dealer only. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained as the manual says.
  • A removed serial number or testing label, or any alteration or tampering.
  • Submersion, long periods of dampness or condensation, or water damage from improper venting.
  • Not covered: normal wear and tear, discoloration and minor noise, chimney parts and non-Hussong accessories, or how well it heats your space.

specInput.html:

Natural gas min18,500 Btu/h (5.42 kW)
Propane max59,500 Btu/h (17.44 kW)
Propane min21,500 Btu/h (6.3 kW)

Orifice sizes (DMS)

Natural gasCenter burner #33 · side burners #51
PropaneCenter burner 1.90mm · side burners #63

Fuel conversion

Built for natural gas. The propane conversion kit is LCK-BH52-SPB (natural gas kit NCK-BH52-SPB), sold separately. Converting is easier before framing in; after installation the control board has to come out (section 8.5, p. 53). Finish the conversion before installing the panels, log set or light-kit parts.

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high-altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m).

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas min5" WC (1.25 kPa)
Natural gas recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
Natural gas max10.5" WC (2.62 kPa)
Propane min12" WC (2.99 kPa)
Propane recommended12" WC (2.99 kPa) (Table 5.1)
Propane max13" WC (3.24 kPa)

Table 5.1 prints "recommended" under the propane 12" WC value; Table 11.1 (p. 65) lists propane as 12" – 13" WC min – max.

Testing

  • Test at the valve's IN tap with a manometer on a ¼" (6mm) I.D. hose, with all other gas appliances in the house on or at full capacity. Light pilot and burner; the reading must fall between the minimum and maximum.
  • Afterwards tighten the tap snug (don't over-tighten), relight, and confirm with the manometer that it reads no pressure.
  • Too high or too low? Contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure.
  • System pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi (3.5 kPa) or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas low / high1.1" / 3.8" WC (0.27 / 0.95 kPa)
Propane low / high2.9" / 11" WC (0.72 / 2.74 kPa)

Manifold test (OUT tap)

  1. Light the pilot. Loosen the OUT tap screw counterclockwise.
  2. Attach the manometer with a ¼" (6mm) I.D. hose, light the burner and read it.
  3. Turn burner and pilot off, remove the hose and tighten the tap clockwise until snug. Don't over-tighten.
  4. Reattach the manometer to confirm the tap is sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Both pressure taps are built into the valve: OUT measures outgoing (manifold) pressure, IN measures incoming pressure.

Standard installation: mantels, hearth, facing

  • Combustible mantels may grow 1" (25mm) deeper for every 1" (25mm) higher, starting at the 6" (152mm) mantel.
  • Non-combustible mantel: at least 6" (152mm) above the top finishing edge for up to 6" (152mm) of depth, then 1" (25mm) up for every 1" (25mm) deeper.
  • 6" (152mm) to any mantel leg, combustible or non-combustible.
  • Floor protection in front isn't required; a combustible hearth may be flush with the bottom finishing edge.
  • Non-combustible material is required at the top and sides, up to 1/2" (13mm) thick; the minimum areas are shown as a drawing (Figure 4.5, p. 34).

Vent pipe: 1" (25mm) on all sides of vertical pipe and on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe; 11" (279mm) from any venting to the enclosure top on horizontal terminations. Vented cavity and KZK installations have their own facing and mantel clearances (Figure 4.7, p. 37).

conflicts.issue: Rough opening width: Table 3.1 gives 65-5/8" (1667mm) (p. 14), as do Figure 3.5 (p. 15) and Figure 4.4 (p. 33), but Figure 3.4 on p. 14 labels the same 1667mm dimension 66 5/8" (three times).

Venturi direction for blue, lifting flames: 11.2.1 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and Table 11.4 says to close the venturi for short, blue flames (p. 66); the troubleshooting chart says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner (p. 69). Table 11.4 also lists lifting (ghosting) flames as venturi closed too far, open slightly.

Access to the ON/OFF switch and remote learn/sync button on the left side: 10.2 says remove the safety barrier screen, glass frame assembly and gas valve access cover plate; 10.3 says remove the safety barrier screen only (both p. 59). 8.2 removes the glass frame before the gas valve access cover (p. 47), while 10.9.11.1 reaches the ember-bed knob by removing only the safety screen and gas valve access cover (p. 64).

Glass latch location: 8.1.1 says (4) spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox secure the glass assembly (p. 47; Figure 8.1 'top latch assembly'), while the 13.1 annual firebox check says to inspect and operate the bottom latch assembly (p. 70).

review.notes: Manual pages 2, 4, 6 and 75 have no text (QA warns about them; no PAGEREF points there). The manual covers models BHM-52 and BHM-52-BW (cover, p. 1) and never says how they differ; the guide lists both and treats them as one. The catalog lists only BHM-52. Not in the manual, so not checked against the catalog: efficiency (65.91% NG / 66.61% LP AFUE), weight (510 lb), heating area. Figure 2.1 (p. 9) gives the appliance dimensions only as unlabeled drawing callouts (41¼", 58⅝", 26 9/16", 28¾", 65⅝", 52 7/16", 30 7/8"…); the catalog H/W/D (41.25 / 58.625 / 26.5625) and view area (52 7/16" x 30 7/8") match numbers in that drawing, but the text doesn't say which callout is which, so they weren't compared and the guide points to the drawing instead. The only glass size in the text is the 29.75" x 49.75" glass part 701-050T (p. 72). Not transcribed (drawings only): Figure 3.4 corner-installation dimensions (p. 14), Figure 3.7 wall pass-through framing (73" callout, p. 17), Figures 4.1–4.5 finishing dimensions (pp. 30–34), the vented cavity overhang figures (pp. 25–28), the Figure 6.1 12" callout at the vertical cap (p. 40) and the Figure 7.2 combination-venting area (p. 46). Table 5.1 (p. 39) prints "recommended" under the propane 12" WC minimum with no separate value, while Table 11.1 (p. 65) lists propane 12"–13" WC min–max; the inlet drawer shows both as printed. Wording problems left out of the guide: 10.9.5 "Turn OFF the appliance" (p. 62) repeats the turn-on wording ("With the system in the OFF position… to turn ON"), so the guide uses 10.7.1.2's "press the remote control ON/OFF key to turn the system OFF" (p. 60) plus 10.9.5's described result; 10.3 numbers two steps "1." (p. 59); the split-flow steps are numbered 4–6 (p. 63); the fan text says "when the fireplace is let" (p. 63). 10.3 says synchronization with the remote is "closed" during manual-operation setup without saying whether the remote must be re-paired afterwards; the guide doesn't claim either way. Lifting/ghosting flames have two remedies in the manual, venturi (Table 11.4, p. 66) or less vent restriction (Table 11.5, p. 67); the guide gives both. The catalog calls the fan kit, top accent light and ember-bed light standard; the manual doesn't say standard or optional (ember-bed bulbs "included in component packet", top-light bulbs "included with this kit", fan assembly BH52-028 listed under "FAN KIT"), so that wasn't flagged as a mismatch. Referenced or summarized, not reproduced: flame-modulation, light-modulation and thermostat deactivation procedures (pp. 62–64), control board removal and installation (pp. 53–54), vented cavity / KZK framing details (pp. 21–28, 36–38), Massachusetts sidewall-vent CO-detector and signage rules (p. 7), the vent-cap part-number tables (p. 42) and the parts list (pp. 72–73). Catalog values that match the manual: input NG 59,500 / 18,500 and LP 59,500 / 21,500 Btu/h (p. 8); 5" x 8" venting, reducible to 4" x 6-5/8" (p. 42); IPI ignition with a CPI option (p. 61); traditional and birchwood log sets, plus Chicago brick, ledgestone, herringbone and black glass panel choices (p. 73); safety barrier screen included (p. 10). check_numbers: every number in the guide was found in the manual text.
